o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish برك (bärk). Cognate with Turkmen and Turkish berk, Chuvash парка (park̬a, “hard, healthy”), Yakut бэрт (bert, “great, excellent”), etc.
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ماسه, from Bulgarian ма́са (mása), from Romanian masă, from Latin mēnsa.
From Arabic زَرَافَة (zarāfa), ultimately from Classical Persian زرناپا.

Likely a semi-learned borrowing from Late Old Anatolian Turkish *باتو (batu) that was attested only in compounds in the Ottoman translations of Quran into Old Anatolian Turkish since 1424, from Proto-Turkic *batïg (“west”). Otherwise, directly borrowed from Turkish batı. Likely used since 1960s.
Literally, “those that are given”. Calque of Russian да́нные (dánnyje), ultimately a calque of Latin data.
From qur- + -ğu. The sense 'device' is likely a semantic loan from Russian устро́йство (ustrójstvo). Compare Kazakh құрылғы (qurılğı) and Uyghur قۇرۇلما (qurulma), etc., for a similar development.
From ovunmaq + -dur. Compare Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐽱𐽶𐾀𐽹𐽰𐽲 (ʾʾvytmʾq, “to console a child; to spoil a child”).
